item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-24
item.description: One sentence settles this morning, and it is the shortest institutional sentence of the year. On 2026-10-16, MOFCOM and MOST issued Announcement No. 48, proposing to add 23 AI technologies to the Catalogue of Technologies Prohibited or Restricted from Export — and, in the policy explanation, stating that open-source release is an export form: a restricted technology released as open source now needs a licence, a prohibited one may not be released at all. Technologies already public through open-source release or academic publication are excluded; future ones require an automatic licence. Two firms walked through the registration gate eight days later — MiniMax by market announcement on 2026-10-23, DeepSeek named by state media the same day — and the market read it as permission rather than as gate. Meanwhile, on 2026-09-07 the Supreme People's Court issued Article XIII of its AI Opinions: a free open-source module with publicly explained functions and security risks may escape tort liability downstream. Two instruments, thirty-nine days and several ministries apart, arrive at opposite conclusions about what publication does. One treats it as the moment control is released; the other as the moment responsibility is released. And on 2026-11-20, at Zhengzhou, the OpenAtom Foundation thanked 32 developers from 23 projects, chosen from 12 months of verifiable contribution records — the first time this ecosystem has produced a participation metric that could in principle be checked.
